meta.description: Select colormaps and qualitative palettes for scientific figures using perceptual uniformity, color-vision-deficiency safety, luminance behavior, data semantics, explicit non-finite handling, and a compact response contract.
meta.audit_type: independent round-two re-audit after follow-up fix
meta.execution_note: Executed all seven archived scored inputs plus a two-case round-two stress input (nine distinct cases total). All 40 assertions passed and all nine PNGs were pixel-checked and opened. R runs reached PASS sentinels and emitted checked outputs before the shared launcher returned 2816; a base-R probe exited 0 while a ggplot2-only probe reproduced exit 2816, separating package teardown from Skill execution. Provider HEAD, status, and SHA-256 hashes were identical before and after.

scientific_integrity.detail: All centers, bounds, distances, mask counts, normalization results, and image properties were computed from saved synthetic fixtures or installed palette implementations.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill selects scientific figure encodings and makes no diagnosis, prescription, treatment recommendation, or participant-level inference.

methodological_ground.detail: Palette types match data semantics; quantitative references, robust bounds, non-finite masking, CVD checks, grayscale testing, and redundant encodings are kept distinct.

code_usability.detail: R and Python code parsed, reached PASS sentinels, satisfied all assertions, and emitted nine non-blank checked artifacts. The post-success R exit is independently reproducible with ggplot2 alone and is not a Skill failure.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4, correctness 4, appropriateness 4. Sequential, diverging, cyclic, categorical, CVD, grayscale, many-group, nonzero-reference, and missing-value workflows are complete and consistent.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 4, error reporting 3, recoverability 4. Non-finite values are explicitly masked and invalid diverging bounds are rejected; underlying library errors remain plain rather than structured.

performance_context.note: Token cost 4, efficiency 4. SKILL.md is 283 lines, the guide routes instead of duplicating, and executable depth remains in examples/tests.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4, consistency 4, feedback design 4, error prevention 4. The seven-field response checklist makes completion and verification observable.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 4, forgiveness 4. Natural prompts cover standard cases, while arbitrary references and NaN/infinity handling are explicit.

security.note: Credential safety 4, input validation 4, data safety 4. There are no secrets, raw-string execution, network calls, destructive operations, or data-retention hazards; bounds and finite values are checked.

maintainability.note: Modularity 4, modifiability 4, testability 4. A concise guide, self-contained examples, and focused R/Python contract tests cleanly separate responsibilities.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision 4, progressive disclosure 4, composability 4, idempotency 4, escape hatches 3. The response contract creates a clean integration seam; broad stop/handoff guidance is naturally limited for this advisory visualization Skill.

inputs.label: Named Okabe-Ito mapping for seven cell types plus unassigned
inputs.note: A named seven-color Okabe-Ito mapping plus Unassigned=#BBBBBB remained stable after T cells were removed. Unassigned also used a cross marker. R CIELAB minima after deutan/protan/tritan transforms were 14.93/20.71/16.17.

assertions.text: Every category is assigned through a named mapping and Unassigned is light grey
assertions.note: Seven chromatic names plus Unassigned=#BBBBBB were present.

assertions.text: Removing T cells does not recolor any remaining category
assertions.note: Full and subset ggplot_build mappings were identical for shared levels.

assertions.text: All three CVD simulations produce finite positive minimum distances
assertions.note: R minima were 14.93, 20.71, and 16.17; Python independently returned 14.17, 13.96, and 10.97.

assertions.text: A redundant non-color encoding distinguishes the reserve class
assertions.note: Unassigned uses marker 4 while chromatic categories use marker 16.

assertions.text: The full and subset plots render non-blank with readable legends
assertions.note: The opened figure showed stable colors, the grey cross class, and complete legends.

inputs.label: vik log-fold-change heatmap with symmetric q99 bounds
inputs.note: The q99 absolute-LFC bound was 4.814764. vik sampled #EBE5E0 at the centre, while the odd 101-color custom ramp sampled #FFFFFF exactly; both arms and the neutral region remained visible.

assertions.text: Bounds are symmetric at plus/minus the 99th percentile of absolute LFC
assertions.note: The computed limits were -4.814764 and +4.814764.

assertions.text: Zero is anchored at the built-in vik centre
assertions.note: midpoint=0 and symmetric limits place zero at #EBE5E0.

assertions.text: The output does not mislabel vik's centre as pure white
assertions.note: The measured near-neutral centre is reported explicitly.

assertions.text: A custom ramp can deliberately sample exact white at zero
assertions.note: The 101-color custom ramp's 51st color was #FFFFFF.

assertions.text: Both diverging arms and the neutral region are visually legible
assertions.note: The opened heatmaps showed the positive block, negative block, and midpoint without blank panels.

inputs.label: CVD and grayscale audit of sequential and rainbow-like candidates
inputs.note: The actual batlow palette remained luminance-monotonic after desaturation; turbo rose then fell in L*. All three CVD transformations returned finite positive distances and the six swatches rendered correctly.

assertions.text: The grayscale check desaturates the actual palette
assertions.note: colorspace::desaturate(batlow) was rendered, not a generic grey ramp.

assertions.text: batlow has monotonic CIELAB lightness
assertions.note: All successive L* differences had one direction.

assertions.text: turbo is not presented as luminance-monotonic
assertions.note: The regression asserted that turbo L* rises and then falls.

assertions.text: The CVD code performs all three simulations and reports distances
assertions.note: Both R and Python produced finite minima for deutan/protan/tritan variants.

assertions.text: The simulated and grayscale panels are visually inspectable
assertions.note: The opened figure showed six labeled, populated swatches and turbo's light-dark reversal.

inputs.note: The migration used batlow for magnitude, vik with symmetric q99=5.956655 for signed data, and romaO for phase. Zero normalized to 0.5; tested cyclic seams stayed below two CAM02-UCS units.

assertions.text: The sequential panel no longer uses jet or rainbow
assertions.note: It uses cmcrameri batlow.

assertions.text: The signed panel uses a diverging palette and symmetric data-derived limits
assertions.note: vik uses plus/minus q99 and maps zero to 0.5.

assertions.text: The phase panel uses a cyclic palette
assertions.note: romaO is used from zero to 2*pi.

assertions.text: Cyclic endpoints close without an artificial seam
assertions.note: romaO, vikO, and twilight endpoint distances were each below two CAM02-UCS units.

assertions.text: All three panels render with visible data and color bars
assertions.note: The opened output contained three populated, appropriately encoded panels.

assertions.text: The four-panel example follows the current guidance

assertions.text: Journal palettes are not claimed as universal accessibility defaults
assertions.note: Measured deutan minima were npg 9.66, aaas 8.96, and lancet 7.51.

assertions.text: The 15-group request is not answered with a supposedly CVD-safe hue-only palette
assertions.note: tab20, Paired, and Set3 each had a deutan minimum below 10.

assertions.text: The representative shipped example is visually sound
assertions.note: The opened four-panel figure was populated and its categorical identities stayed stable.

inputs.label: Thirty clusters with a request for hue-only identity colors
inputs.note: The response declined the false accessibility promise and produced 30 directly labeled facets using one accessible accent. All clusters remained represented without smuggling identity back into hue.

assertions.text: The output refuses the false promise of 30 CVD-safe identity hues
assertions.note: Hue-only encoding beyond eight groups is identified as unsafe.

assertions.text: A practical redundant alternative is produced
assertions.note: The plot uses direct facet labels.

assertions.text: All 30 clusters remain represented
assertions.note: The factor has 30 levels and the opened plot has 30 labeled facets.

assertions.text: The alternative does not smuggle identity back into hue
assertions.note: ggplot_build found exactly one point color across all facets.

assertions.text: The 30-panel output is visually inspectable
assertions.note: The opened output showed populated C01-C30 facets with readable labels.

inputs.label: Nonzero 0.5 reference with missing matrix cells
inputs.note: TwoSlopeNorm mapped the declared reference to 0.5, 48 missing cells stayed masked, and #BBBBBB separated missingness from the quantitative palette. The opened figure showed distinct white-reference and grey-missing regions.

assertions.text: The 0.5 scientific reference maps to the diverging centre
assertions.note: TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.5) returns 0.5 at the reference.

assertions.text: Missing values are not silently mapped to a quantitative color
assertions.note: The copied colormap uses #BBBBBB as its bad color.

assertions.text: All missing cells are preserved as missing
assertions.note: The mask count is 48, matching the synthetic block.

assertions.text: The response reports reference, bounds, and masked count
assertions.note: The current guidance explicitly requires these fields.

assertions.text: Reference and missing regions are visually distinct
assertions.note: The opened figure shows the white reference block separately from the grey missing block.

final.grade_note: All Production Ready floors pass: static 98>=80, execution 95.9>=85, Layer 1 average 38.5>=32, Layer 2 average 57.4>=48, assertions 40/40=100%, no veto, no open P0, and no open P1.

key_strengths: The response contract makes palette type, normalization, missingness, CVD behavior, luminance, redundant encoding, and visual verification explicit and machine-checkable.
Arbitrary scientific references and NaN/+Inf/-Inf values are handled without allowing missing data to enter the quantitative color scale.
Categorical identity mappings remain stable across subsets and switch to labels or facets when hue cannot safely carry identity.
Shipped examples and focused tests execute in both R and Python against preserved synthetic fixtures, with nine visually inspected outputs.
